title: Cameron's division of the gifts
source_text: VII. Neque multum abludit distinctio Cameronis tomo primo praelectionum digressione de gratia, ubi dicit gratiae dona quaedam esse quae nullis contingunt, qui iidem non servantur: alia vero quae illis etiam obtingunt qui non servantur. Item Dei dona dividi in ea quae aliis tantum, non etiam nobis prosunt, qualia sunt omnia Dei dona in impios collata: & ea dona quae saepe aliis prosunt, aliquando non prosunt, semper tamen iis prosunt in quos sunt collata, qualia sunt fides, spes, & charitas.
pass_a_gloss: VII. Nor does the distinction of Cameron in the first tome of the lectures in the digression on grace much differ, where he says that there are some gifts of grace which befall none who are not also saved: but others which befall even those who are not saved. Likewise that the gifts of God are divided into those which profit others only, not also us, such as are all the gifts of God conferred on the ungodly: and those gifts which often profit others, sometimes do not profit, yet always profit those on whom they are conferred, such as are faith, hope, and charity.
pass_b_english: Thesis VII. Cameron's distinction, in the digression on grace in the first volume of his lectures, is not far from this either. He says that some gifts of grace come to no one who is not also saved, while others come even to those who are not saved.

He also divides God's gifts into those that help others only and not ourselves, such as all of God's gifts bestowed on the ungodly, and those that often help others and sometimes do not, but always help the people on whom they are bestowed. Faith, hope and love are of this second kind.

choices.english: grace freely given ... grace that makes pleasing
choices.why: The scholastic pair (Aquinas, Summa theologiae I-II q. 111 a. 1): gifts given for the good of others versus the grace that makes its bearer pleasing to God. Kept literal because the Reformed objections turn on the very words.
